description:
We are a team of passionate software developers participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We're working on an interactive lunar mission game that helps children learn about space exploration, resource management, and engineering decisions through gameplay.

Our skills include web development, programming, and AI. We welcome creative minds with experience in game development, 3D design, UI/UX, or space science to help us bring this idea to life!
summary: Mars Life Line is a browser game that puts young players in charge of a Martian outpost. Players choose a landing site, restore power and life support, grow food, and respond to a radiation warning. Each choice has a benefit and a cost: backup power helps immediately but leaves the solar panels dusty, while Emergency Mode saves power by pausing crop growth. PEBBLE, the station’s robot companion, helps players understand their next steps. NASA maps, radiation records, and life-support references connect the mission to real science. The game makes the engineering trade-offs of living on Mars interactive and easier to understand.
details:
Mars Life Line — A Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Every watt. Every breath. Every choice.

Mars Life Line is an interactive 3D educational survival game for children aged 7–12, developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Through an immersive Martian mission, young explorers learn how astronauts balance limited resources, solve engineering problems, and make decisions that affect their survival.

01. The Mission: Welcome to ARES-7

A dust storm has damaged ARES-7, a fictional Martian research station. The next crew is on its way, and the player must restore the outpost before they arrive.

Guided by PEBBLE, a friendly robotic companion, players experience seven connected mission scenes involving exploration, equipment repair, resource management, and an emergency response.

02. Every Decision Matters

Survival depends on five interconnected systems: power, water, oxygen, food, and radiation safety.

Players face meaningful engineering trade-offs:

  • Solar Power: Clean dusty solar panels for sustainable electricity or activate limited backup power for immediate support.
  • Life Support: Restore water recycling before restarting oxygen production.
  • Greenhouse: Balance water and energy consumption against crop growth.
  • Radiation Emergency: Conserve power, protect equipment, and reach shelter before exposure becomes dangerous.

Every action has consequences. Resource shortages can interrupt critical systems, while good decisions improve the station's chances of survival.

03. Meet PEBBLE — Your Mission Companion

PEBBLE guides players through mission objectives, explains system failures, and helps them understand the consequences of their choices.

Instead of simply providing answers, PEBBLE connects the player's actions to the scientific concepts behind them.

04. Connecting Gameplay to NASA Science

Mars Life Line incorporates NASA resources to provide scientific context for its educational simulation.

  • NASA/JPL Mars Trek: Mars imagery and topography inform the landing-site experience, introducing Gale Crater, Jezero Crater, and Deuteronilus Mensae.
  • NASA OSDR RadLab: Curiosity radiation observations provide context for the mission's radiation hazards.
  • NASA DONKI: A documented May 2024 solar event inspires the fictional radiation emergency.
  • NASA Life Support BVAD: Published crew water and oxygen requirements inform the game's educational explanations.

The project distinguishes real NASA observations from simplified gameplay values. The outpost, resource rates, and safety thresholds are educational approximations, not validated operational limits.

05. Learning Through Experience

Mars Life Line is designed to develop five essential skills:

  • Resource Management — balancing limited supplies.
  • Systems Thinking — understanding interconnected survival systems.
  • Scientific Decision-Making — comparing solutions and consequences.
  • Risk Management — responding to environmental hazards.
  • Problem-Solving — learning from failure and improving decisions.

At the end of the mission, players receive a report evaluating their decisions and the condition of the outpost.

06. Technology & Validation

Built with React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Rapier, Zustand, and Vite, Mars Life Line runs directly in a desktop browser.

The project includes automated simulation and regression tests covering mission outcomes, resource shortages, equipment failures, and radiation exposure.

Development verification and documented walkthroughs have been completed. Formal usability testing with children has not yet been conducted.

PEBBLE provides built-in guidance without requiring an API key. An optional Gemini-powered mode supports local development testing.

07. AI Tools & Transparency

Our team used ChatGPT, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity, Grok, Manus AI, and ElevenLabs to assist with ideation, development, visual assets, demonstration production, and voice-over.

The team reviewed AI-assisted outputs and made the final design and implementation decisions. AI-generated media must be identified according to the challenge's disclosure requirements.

08. Explore the Project

Play the Game: https://baraa404.github.io/mars-life-line-game/

Source Code: https://github.com/baraa404/mars-life-line-game

Mars Life Line turns space science into something children can explore, experience, and understand—one decision at a time.
